summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide and cyclophosphamide, was admitted with neck pain present for three days, likely musculoskeletal in origin. An MRI of the cervical spine showed slightly worsened spinal stenosis at C3-C4 without cord compression or acute myeloma involvement. During the admission, he developed a fever and was found to have right lower lobe pneumonia on chest imaging, which was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral levofloxacin. He received one unit of PRBCs for symptomatic anemia and was managed for chronic kidney disease and subtherapeutic INR, with warfarin held due to recent nosebleed. His Revlimid was paused due to infection and cytopenias. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to follow up with oncology and spine surgery. Blood cultures remained negative at discharge.
